raw_texts_per_turn:
Below is a 12-week prenatal strength program tailored for a 30-year-old advanced lifter at 20 weeks pregnant, cleared for moderate intensity. It respects contraindications: no supine positions, no maximal attempts, no contact sports. It uses a full gym, emphasizes strength maintenance, posture, pelvic floor, core stability, and prepares for late pregnancy demands. Intensity cues use RPE and breathing/talk test. Include deloads and autoregulation for day-to-day variability.

Global guidelines
- Frequency: 3 strength days/week + 1 optional accessory/mobility day.
- Session length: 50–70 minutes including warm-up and cooldown.
- Intensity: RPE 6–7 most sets (leave 3–4 reps in reserve). No grinders.
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3s) where noted; powerful but crisp concentrics without breath holding.
- Breathing/bracing: Exhale on effort; avoid prolonged Valsalva. Use 360° breath and gentle brace.
- Positioning: No supine after 16 wks—use incline, side-lying, half-kneeling, or standing. Avoid prolonged prone. Manage diastasis risk: no aggressive spinal flexion/rotation under load, no front planks or sit-ups; choose anti-extension/anti-rotation.
- Transverse plane and single-leg: Maintain gait mechanics and pelvic control.
- Rest: 60–120s, longer for big lifts as needed.
- Red flags to stop and refer: vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, painful contractions, dizziness/faintness, chest pain, calf pain/swelling, shortness of breath at rest, decreased fetal movement once perceivable.

Warm-up template (10–12 min each session)
- Breath/pelvic floor: 2–3 minutes 360° diaphragmatic breathing with 3–5 gentle Kegel contractions coordinated with exhale, full relax on inhale.
- Mobility: Cat-cow to neutral, open-books (side-lying), thoracic rotations in quadruped, 90/90 hip switches.
- Dynamic prep: Bodyweight sit-to-stand, heel-elevated squats, banded lateral walks, scapular wall slides.
- Ramps: 2–3 progressive warm-up sets for first two compound lifts.

Core and pelvic floor
- Core focus is anti-extension/anti-rotation: dead bug variations (incline bench), tall/half-kneeling cable pressouts, Pallof press holds, suitcase carries, heel slides.
- Pelvic floor: 3–4 days/week, 5–8 gentle contractions/day, 3–5s hold, 6–8s relax. Add 3–5 quick flicks. Avoid overtraining; emphasize full relaxation.

Programming overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4, gestational weeks ~20–23): Strength maintenance and posture. Moderate volume, bilateral + unilateral patterns, machine/incline swaps for supine.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8, ~24–27): Emphasize unilateral strength, stability, hinge/squat variants with more support, manage bump-related ROM changes. Slight deload in Week 6.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12, ~28–31): Reduce axial loading peaks, increase tempo/isometric control, maintain strength with lower intensities. Deload in Week 11. Prep for third trimester comfort strategies.

Weekly structure
- Day A: Lower emphasis + push accessory + core
- Day B: Upper emphasis + hinge accessory + core
- Day C: Mixed total-body + carries + conditioning
- Optional Day D: Mobility/conditioning (low impact)

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4
Focus: Maintain strength, refine breathing/bracing, swap supine to incline/side-lying, introduce anti-rotation core. RPE 6–7.

Week 1
Day A
- Safety bar box squat or goblet squat: 4x5 @ RPE 6
- Split squat (rear foot on low pad if comfortable): 3x8/side
- 45° back extension (neutral spine, hands across chest): 3x10
- Seated cable row (neutral grip): 4x8
- Landmine press (standing or half-kneeling): 4x6/side
- Pallof press hold: 3x20–30s/side

Day B
- Trap-bar deadlift (high handles): 4x4–5 @ RPE 6–7
- Half-kneeling single-arm lat pulldown: 3x10/side
- Machine chest press (slight incline): 4x8
- Tall-kneeling cable face pull + external rotation: 3x12
- Suitcase carry: 4x25–35m/side
- Incline dead bug (bench 30–45°): 3x6/side slow

Day C
- Double kettlebell front rack box squat: 5x5 (moderate)
- Romanian deadlift with straps if grip fatigue: 3x8
- One-arm cable row (split stance): 3x10/side
- Seated DB overhead press (back support): 3x8
- Sled push (light-moderate): 6x20m, walk back
- Side-lying open book breathing: 2x8/side

Optional Day D
- 20–25 min incline treadmill walk or bike + hip/glute mobility + gentle PF series

Week 2
- Progress Week 1 loads 2–3% or 1–2 reps where noted, maintain RPE.
- Swap variations to manage novelty:
  - Day A: Front-foot elevated split squat 3x10/side; sled hamstring curl 3x12
  - Day B: Rack pull from knee 4x5; single-arm cable chest press 3x10/side
  - Day C: Landmine goblet squat 4x6; KB deadlift 3x10; farmer carry 4x30m

Week 3
- Slight volume bump:
  - Big lift sets become 5x4–5 at same RPE
  - Accessory 3–4 sets of 8–12
- Add anti-rotation march: Cable Pallof march 3x8/side
- Keep conditioning as steady-state 15–20 min post or separate day.

Week 4
- Consolidate: Keep Week 3 volume but hold loads or reduce 2% to stay at RPE 6–7.
- Technique emphasis: Tempo 3–1–1 on RDL and split squats.
- Monitor diastasis cues during pushing; regress if coning/doming appears.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8
Focus: Unilateral strength and pelvic control, slightly more support, manage ROM, keep intensity moderate. Built-in deload Week 6.

Week 5
Day A
- Safety bar box squat to parallel box: 4x4–5
- Walking lunge (shorter stride for pelvic comfort): 3x10/side
- Hip thrust on bench set to incline (torso supported, no supine flat): 4x8
- Chest-supported row: 4x8
- Half-kneeling landmine press: 4x6/side
- Pallof iso with step-out: 3x15–20s/side

Day B
- Trap-bar deadlift: 5x3–4 (crisp reps)
- Single-leg RDL (DB, slider or kickstand as needed): 3x8/side
- Assisted pull-up (band or machine): 4x6–8
- Incline machine chest press: 3x10
- Suitcase carry with march: 4x20–30m or 3x12 marches/side
- Heel slides with mini-band (incline): 3x8/side

Day C
- Landmine squat to target: 5x5
- Cable row (one-and-a-half reps): 3x10
- Seated DB shoulder press (back-supported): 3x8–10
- Sled push: 6–8x15–20m
- Side-lying clamshell or banded hip abduction: 3x15/side
- Tall-kneeling anti-extension pressout: 3x10

Week 6 (Deload)
- Reduce sets by ~30–40% and/or loads by ~5–10%. Keep movement quality.
- Replace heavy hinge with KB swings light-to-moderate if comfortable and no symptoms, or stick to RDL 3x8 light.
- Keep carries short and easy.
- Add extra mobility and breath work.

Here’s a practical, pregnancy-safe nutrition plan to support maternal health and maintain lean mass for a 30-year-old advanced lifter at 20–31 weeks. Guiding principles
- Energy: Eat enough to support pregnancy and training without aggressive surplus. Expect stable weight gain in 2nd–3rd trimester per OB guidance.
  - Trimester add-ons (general): +300–350 kcal/day in 2nd trimester; +450 kcal/day in 3rd. Adjust to appetite, weight gain trajectory, and session demand.
  - Practical: Start with +300 kcal/day above her pre-pregnancy maintenance. Track weekly trends; adjust ±100–150 kcal to keep weight gain on target.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day to support lean mass and fetal growth.
  - Distribute 20–35 g high-quality protein across 4–5 feedings/day.
  - Include leucine-rich sources to stimulate muscle protein synthesis.
- Carbohydrates: 3–5 g/kg/day, bias around training to fuel performance and recovery.
  - Higher end (4.5–5 g/kg) on heavier training days; lower end (3–4 g/kg) on rest/deload days.
- Fats: 25–35% of total calories from fats, emphasizing mono- and polyunsaturated fats; include omega-3s.
- Hydration: Aim for clear to pale-yellow urine. Baseline ~2.3–2.7 L fluid/day plus sweat losses; add ~300–500 mL around training. Include electrolytes if sweating heavily.

Key micronutrients and supplements (confirm with OB)
- Prenatal vitamin: Daily, covering folate (as methylfolate or folic acid), iodine, vitamin D, iron (if indicated), B12, and others.
- Iron: Test and supplement if low or if advised. Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C to enhance absorption; avoid taking iron with calcium-rich foods.
- Vitamin D: Often 1,000–2,000 IU/day if levels are low/insufficient (per lab work and OB guidance).
- Choline: Target ~450 mg/day (eggs, lean meats, soy). Consider choline bitartrate if intake is low.
- Omega-3 DHA/EPA: ~200–300 mg DHA/day (via low-mercury fish 1–2x/week or algae oil).
- Calcium: ~1,000 mg/day via dairy/fortified alternatives, leafy greens, tofu with calcium sulfate.
- Magnesium: Food-first; consider gentle glycinate form if cramping/sleep issues (confirm with OB).
- Avoid: High-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, king mackerel, tilefish), unpasteurized dairy/juices, undercooked meats/eggs, deli meats unless heated, alcohol. Limit high-caffeine to ≤200 mg/day.

Meal timing and training nutrition
- Pre-training (60–120 minutes before):
  - 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein + fluid.
  - Examples: Greek yogurt with honey and berries; turkey-and-jam sandwich on sourdough; oats with banana and whey isolate (pregnancy-safe brand).
- During training (if sessions >60 minutes, warm environment, or heavy sweating):
  - 250–500 mL water every 15–20 min; consider 10–20 g easily digestible carbs (sports drink) if needed.
- Post-training (within 1–2 hours):
  - 25–35 g protein + 60–90 g carbs + fluid/electrolytes.
  - Examples: Rice bowl with salmon/tofu, veggies, avocado; smoothie with milk, banana, oats, peanut butter, protein.
- Even protein distribution:
  - Anchor breakfast and lunch with ≥25–30 g protein.
  - Include a protein-forward evening snack if total daily protein is lagging.

Daily template (example for 70 kg athlete; adjust portions to targets)
- Target macros (training day, mid-2nd trimester): ~2,300–2,500 kcal; Protein 95–110 g (1.35–1.55 g/kg), Carbs 260–320 g (3.7–4.6 g/kg), Fat 70–85 g (27–31% kcal). Increase by ~100–200 kcal as pregnancy progresses or if weight gain is below target.
- Breakfast:
  - Option A: 2 eggs + 200 g Greek yogurt, berries, honey; 2 slices wholegrain toast with butter or avocado.
  - Option B: Oats cooked in milk, banana, chia seeds, whey isolate; side of kiwi.
- Snack:
  - Cottage cheese + pineapple + granola; or hummus with wholegrain pita and carrots.
- Lunch:
  - Grain bowl: quinoa or rice, 120–150 g chicken/salmon/tempeh, mixed veggies, olive oil vinaigrette, feta (pasteurized).
- Pre-training snack (if lunch was >3 h prior):
  - Yogurt + granola; or banana + peanut butter + chocolate milk.
- Post-training/dinner:
  - Lean beef/turkey/soy mince tacos on corn tortillas, beans, salsa, cheese; side salad with olive oil.
  - Or baked tofu/salmon, roasted potatoes, vegetables, tahini.
- Evening snack:
  - Milk/cocoa + banana bread; or protein smoothie with oats and berries.

Lean-mass support strategies
- Hit protein minimum daily; prioritize chewable whole-food proteins first, then add a high-quality protein powder if needed to meet targets. Whey or whey/casein blends are effective; plant blends (pea/rice) if dairy-averse.
- Include 2–3 leucine-rich feedings/day (e.g., 25–30 g whey, 120–150 g chicken/fish, 3 eggs + dairy).
- Pair protein with carbs after lifting to reduce muscle protein breakdown and replenish glycogen.
- Use creatine monohydrate only with explicit OB approval; evidence in pregnancy is limited. If approved, 3 g/day with plenty of fluids.
- Avoid aggressive dieting or intermittent fasting; prioritize steady energy and regular meals.

Gastrointestinal comfort and nausea management
- Small, frequent meals (every 3–4 hours).
- Choose easy-to-digest carbs pre-workout: ripe banana, rice cakes, oats, yogurt.

Fiber and bowel regularity
- Aim 25–30 g/day with adequate fluids. Include oats, berries, legumes, chia/flax, vegetables. Increase gradually if currently low.

Sodium and electrolytes
- Don’t aggressively restrict sodium; include salted foods/electrolytes on heavy sweat days, especially in hot weather.

- Track: energy, appetite, training performance, recovery, body weight, and any GI or reflux symptoms.
- If appetite low but protein target unmet: add liquid calories (smoothies, milk, drinkable yogurt).
- If weight gain exceeds OB targets with good energy: reduce added fats/oils and discretionary snacks first; keep protein steady.
- If performance lags and RPEs climb: add 30–60 g carbs pre-lift and/or +100–150 kcal/day.

Food safety and sourcing
- Prioritize pasteurized dairy, well-cooked meats/eggs, thoroughly washed produce.
- Choose low-mercury fish: salmon, trout, sardines, pollock, shrimp (1–2 servings/week).
- Maintain kitchen hygiene and cold-chain for perishables.

Here’s a prenatal-safe cardio plan to layer onto the 12-week strength program. It complements strength, supports cardiovascular health, energy, and recovery without excessive fatigue or overheating.

Global cardio guidelines
- Frequency: 2–4 days/week, adjusted to how she feels and strength day demands.
- Intensity: Mostly conversational pace (RPE 4–5), avoiding breath-holding and overheating. Short moderate pickups if symptom-free.
- Duration: 20–35 minutes/session most days; up to 40 minutes if feeling great. Start at the low end and progress gradually.
- Monitoring: Use talk test, RPE, and symptom check. Stop if dizzy, chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, painful contractions, or calf pain/swelling.
- Environment: Cool, ventilated space; hydrate before/during/after. Avoid hot, humid conditions.
- Modality options (low impact): Incline treadmill walk, cycling (upright or recumbent), elliptical, rowing (short strokes if bump-comfortable), swimming or deep-water jogging, sled pushes (steady, not sprints).
- Pelvic floor: If pelvic girdle or pubic symphysis pain appears, favor cycling, swimming, or elliptical over long walking. Keep strides shorter and cadence higher on walks.

Weekly structure
- Pair 2 cardio sessions on non-lifting days and 1 short session after an easier lift or as a separate PM session if energy allows.
- Keep one day fully off or just gentle mobility/breathing.

12-week progression
Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4, gestational ~20–23)
- Goal: Establish routine, aerobic base, and temperature management.
- Week 1:
  - Session 1: Incline walk 25 min, RPE 4. Start 3–5% incline if comfortable, 2–3 min easy + 5 x 3 min steady / 2 min easy.
  - Session 2: Bike 20–25 min steady, RPE 4.
  - Optional Session 3: Pool swim or deep-water jog 20–25 min easy, focus on relaxed breathing.
- Week 2:
  - Add 3–5 total minutes across sessions (e.g., walk 28–30 min; bike 25–28 min).
  - Optional: 4 x 45 s brisk pickups during the walk at RPE 5, full 2 min easy between.
- Week 3:
  - Session 1: Elliptical 30 min steady, RPE 4.
  - Session 2: Incline walk 28–30 min with 6 x 1 min brisk, RPE 5, 2 min easy.
  - Optional: Swim 25–30 min continuous or 5 x 3 min with 1 min easy.
- Week 4:
  - Consolidate volume; hold durations and focus on relaxed nasal-inhale/mouth-exhale. If feeling great, add 1–2 min total per session but keep RPE ≤5.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8, ~24–27)
- Goal: Maintain volume, sprinkle in light tempo changes without intensity spikes; built-in deload Week 6 to match lifting.
- Week 5:
  - Session 1: Bike 30–32 min, include 3 x 4 min steady RPE 5 with 3 min easy.
  - Session 2: Walk 30–32 min, 10 min easy + 10 min steady + 10–12 min easy.
  - Optional: Row 20–22 min easy (shorter stroke length) or pool 25–30 min.
- Week 6 (Cardio deload):
  - 2 sessions only, 20–25 min each, RPE 3–4, no pickups. Prioritize swim or bike for comfort.
- Week 7:
  - Session 1: Elliptical 30–35 min steady, RPE 4–5.
  - Session 2: Walk 30–32 min with gentle hills or 6 x 1 min brisk, RPE 5, 2 min easy.
  - Optional: Sled push steady 6–8 x 20 m at easy-moderate pace, long rests; keep HR smooth, not spiky.
- Week 8:
  - Maintain Week 7 or add 2–3 min to one session if recovery is solid. Keep RPE ≤5.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12, ~28–31)
- Goal: Keep cardiovascular fitness while minimizing impact and heat; reduce peaks as belly grows; deload Week 11.
- Week 9:
  - Session 1: Recumbent bike 30–35 min steady, RPE 4.
  - Session 2: Pool 25–30 min continuous or intervals 8 x 2 min easy/1 min steady.
  - Optional: Walk 25–30 min flat route, shorter stride, RPE 4.
- Week 10:
  - Keep two steady-state sessions (bike + pool or elliptical), 28–35 min each at RPE 4–5.
  - If feeling great, add light cadence surges: 6 x 30 s at RPE 5 with 90 s easy on bike only.
- Week 11 (Cardio deload):
  - 2 sessions, 20–25 min easy, RPE 3–4. Prefer pool or bike. No surges.
- Week 12:
  - Session 1: Recumbent bike 28–32 min steady, RPE 4.
  - Session 2: Walk 25–30 min easy-moderate or pool 25–30 min easy, RPE 4.
  - Keep one full rest day.

How to pair with the strength plan
- On strength days: Optional 10–15 min easy cooldown cardio (bike/elliptical) post-lift or separate later in the day.
- On non-strength days: Do the longer cardio sessions.
- Before lifting: If doing cardio first, keep it easy (≤10–12 min, RPE 3–4) as a warm-up only.
- After deload weeks in lifting (Weeks 6 and 11), mirror reduced cardio volume to keep recovery high.

Pelvic floor and comfort considerations
- If pelvic girdle pain arises, swap longer walks for cycling or swimming; avoid long single-leg stance times and steep inclines.
- Keep strides shorter, increase cadence; choose flatter routes and supportive shoes.
- Use belly support band if it improves comfort during longer walks.

Hydration and fueling around cardio
- Hydrate well: 300–500 mL water in the hour before; sip 250–500 mL per 20–30 min during as needed.
- Pre-cardio snack (30–90 min prior): 20–30 g carbs + 10–20 g protein if fasted or hungry (banana + yogurt; toast + nut butter; chocolate milk).
- Post-cardio: Fold into regular meals; include protein 20–30 g and carbs 30–60 g if not lifting that day.

Success metrics and adjustments
- Signs to maintain/advance: Conversational pace maintained, good sleep, steady energy, no pelvic or low back flare-ups.
- Signs to pull back: Rising RPE at same pace, overheating, increased swelling, pelvic heaviness, or any red-flag symptoms—reduce duration by 20–30%, choose cooler/low-impact modes, and consult OB if symptoms persist.

Short answer: No—she shouldn’t test a true 1RM in Week 12. Max attempts are contraindicated in pregnancy due to high intra-abdominal pressure, breath holding risk, and unpredictable fatigue/ligament laxity. We can still give her a satisfying “peak” week that feels like testing while staying submaximal and safe.

Week 12 “peak” strategy (safe, satisfying, and specific)
Goal: Showcase strength, move heavier singles/doubles with great speed, then estimate 1RM from submax sets. Keep RPE ≤8, no grinders, no prolonged Valsalva, and use supported positions (no flat supine).

Global rules for peak week
- Top exposures: 1–3 singles at RPE 7–8 (crisp bar speed), or 1–2 doubles @ RPE 7.
- Back-off: 1–2 sets of 3–5 @ RPE 6–7 for reinforcement.
- Estimation: Use E1RM from rep PRs at submax loads (e.g., E1RM = Load × (1 + reps/30) for sets at RPE ≤8).
- Safeguards: Spotters/safeties set; exhale through sticking point; stop any set if speed drops markedly, symptoms appear, or you need to breath-hold.

Example Week 12 sessions

Day A (Squat pattern + press)
- Hatfield or SSB box squat
  - Warm-ups to single @ RPE 7, then single @ RPE 8 if clean
  - Back-off 2x3 @ RPE 6–7
  - E1RM from the RPE 7–8 single and/or a 3RM-equivalent back-off
- Incline machine or DB press
  - 1–2 top sets: 1–2 reps @ RPE 7–8
  - Back-off 2x4–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Core/carry: Suitcase carry 3x20–25 m/side; Pallof press 2x20s/side

Day B (Hinge + upper pull/press)
- Trap-bar deadlift (high handles) or block pulls below knee
  - Work to single @ RPE 7, optional single @ RPE 8
  - Back-off 2x2–3 @ RPE 6–7
  - Estimate 1RM from the single
- Assisted pull-up or lat pulldown: 3x6–8 @ RPE 7
- Seated or landmine press: 3x5–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Core: Incline dead bug 2x5/side; offset carry 2x20 m/side

Day C (Total body showcase)
- Landmine squat to target
  - 2x2 @ RPE 7–8, then 1x3–5 @ RPE 6–7
- RDL: 2x4–6 @ RPE 6–7 with 2–3s eccentric
- Row + shoulders: 2–3x8 each, moderate
- Conditioning finisher: Optional 5–6 min easy sled pushes

How to scratch the “test” itch without maxing
- AMRAP-at-RPE-8: Choose a safe lift (e.g., landmine press, chest-supported row, leg press). Do one hard set at RPE 8, leaving 2 reps in reserve. Use it to estimate a rep PR, not absolute max.
- Velocity stop: If you have a bar speed device, cap singles when velocity drops >10–15% from your best warm-up single of the day.
- Rep targets: Hit a clean double at the heaviest load you’ve used this cycle (RPE ≤8). That’s a legit achievement in pregnancy.

What to avoid in “peak” week
- True 1RM attempts, grinders, or breath-held bracing.
- Flat supine bench. Use 15–30° incline if benching.
- New exercises or ROM extremes just to chase numbers.
- Fatigue stacking: Keep accessories brief; prioritize sleep, hydration, carbs.

Fueling and recovery in peak week
- Increase carbs slightly (+30–60 g/day vs normal) to support heavy singles/doubles.
- Pre-lift: 30–50 g carbs + 20–25 g protein 60–90 min prior.
- Post-lift: 25–35 g protein + 60–90 g carbs.
- Hydration and cool environment; avoid overheating.
- Keep cardio light-moderate, 2 sessions of 20–25 min at RPE 3–4.

If she really wants a concrete number
- Use E1RM from a smooth single at RPE 8 or a submax set:
  - Example: Single at 120 kg @ RPE 8 with speed → E1RM ≈ 120 / (1 – 0.06 to 0.08) ≈ 128–130 kg (depending on model).
  - Or 5 reps at 90 kg @ RPE 8 → E1RM ≈ 90 × (1 + 5/30) ≈ 105 kg.
- Record these “paper PRs” and revisit true testing postpartum with medical clearance.

Bottom line
- No max testing in Week 12. Instead, execute a controlled showcase with submax singles/doubles, then estimate 1RM. She’ll feel challenged, see objective numbers, and stay within prenatal safety.

- Trap-bar deadlift
  - Top set 3 @ RPE 7–8; back-off 3x3 @ RPE 6–7
- Single-arm cable pulldown (half-kneeling): 4x8/side heavy
- Press: Incline DB press (30–45°, neutral, spotter): 4x6–8 @ RPE 7
- Cable face pull + ER: 3x12–15
- Suitcase carry heavy: 4x30 m/side
- Core: Heel slides (incline) with band 3x8/side

Finisher: Row erg 5 x 45 s steady-hard (RPE 6) / 75 s easy

Day C
- Landmine reverse lunge: 4x6/side @ RPE 7–8 (short stride)
- RDL: 4x6 @ 3 s eccentric, RPE 7
- Press: Seated Arnold press: 4x6–8 @ RPE 7
- Cable row (1 s squeeze): 3x10 heavy
- Core: Modified side plank on knees or bear hover breathing 3x20–30 s/side (swap to Pallof hold if any doming)

Cardio (Week 7)
- Elliptical 30–35 min steady RPE 4–5
- Walk 30–32 min with gentle hills or 6 x 1 min brisk (RPE 5), 2 min easy
- Optional sled steady 6–8 x 20 m

Week 8
- Progress Week 7 by +2–3% load or +1 rep where RPE allows.
- Cluster/pauses:
  - Hatfield squat: 4x(2+2) @ RPE 7, 20–30 s intra-set rest
  - Trap-bar DL: 4x3 with 2 s pause just off floor each rep
- Accessories at RPE 7 with tempos.
- Pressing:
  - Day A: Landmine press clusters 4x(2+2) @ RPE 7
  - Day B: Incline machine press top set 6 @ RPE 7–8; back-off 3x6 @ RPE 6–7
  - Day C: Seated DB overhead press 3x6–8 @ RPE 7

Cardio (Week 8)
- Maintain Week 7 or add 2–3 min to one session; optional bike 30 min with 6 x 45 s brisk (RPE 5–6) / 90 s easy if recovery is good.

PHASE 3 (Weeks 9–12, ~28–31 weeks): Maintain strength, reduce axial peaks, tempo/isometrics, safe “peak” in Week 12
Keep RPE mostly 6–7; select supported positions. Deload Week 11. Peak Week 12 uses submax singles/doubles and estimated 1RMs—no true maxing.

Week 9
Day A
- Hatfield squat (to box): 5x4 @ RPE 6
- Leg press (ROM to comfort): 4x8
- 45° back extension light: 3x10
- Row: Chest-supported row 4x8–10
- Press: Half-kneeling landmine press with 2 s pause 3x6/side
- Core: Pallof ISO 3x25–30s/side; offset carry (front rack + suitcase) 3x20 m/side

Day B
- Block pull (below knee): 5x3–4 smooth
- Single-leg press or low step-up: 3x10/side
- Lat pulldown neutral: 4x8–10
- Press: Incline machine chest press 3x10
- Suitcase or offset carry: 4x20–30 m/side
- Core: Incline dead bug with band anti-rotation 3x6/side

Day C
- Landmine squat to target: 4x6
- DB RDL 3 s eccentric: 3x8
- Seated cable row 1 s squeeze: 3x10
- Press: Seated DB overhead press light-moderate 3x8
- Core: Side-lying hip abduction 3x12/side; farmer carry 3x20–25 m

Cardio (Week 9)
- Recumbent bike 30–35 min steady RPE 4
- Pool 25–30 min continuous or 8 x 2 min easy/1 min steady
- Optional flat walk 25–30 min RPE 4

Week 10
- Maintain patterns; introduce submax density/pauses.
Day A
- Hatfield squat 4x(2+2) @ RPE 6–7
- Leg press 3x10
- Press: Landmine press 4x5–6 @ RPE 7
- Core: Pallof pressouts 3x10; suitcase carry 3x20–25 m/side

Day B
- Block pull 4x3 with 2 s pause just off blocks
- Lat pulldown 4x8–10
- Press: Incline DB press 3x8 @ RPE 6–7
- Core: Standing anti-rotation hold 2x30–40 s/side; side-lying clamshell 3x12–15/side

Day C
- Landmine squat 4x6
- DB RDL 3x8
- Seated row 3x10
- Press: Machine shoulder press 3x8–10
- Core: Tall-kneeling pressout 3x8

Cardio (Week 10)
- Two steady sessions (bike + pool/elliptical), 28–35 min RPE 4–5. Optional bike 6 x 30 s cadence surges (RPE 5) if symptom-free.

Week 11 (Deload)
- Swap big barbell lifts for supported machines; reduce sets 40–50%.
Day A
- Leg press 3x10 light
- Chest-supported row 3x10 light
- Press: Incline machine press 3x10 light
- Core: Incline dead bug 2x5/side; Pallof press 2x8/side

Day B
- Cable pull-through 3x12 light
- Seated row 3x10 light
- Press: Machine shoulder press 2–3x10 light
- Core: Suitcase carry 2x20 m/side; side-lying abduction 2x12/side

Day C
- Landmine squat 3x6 easy
- DB RDL 2–3x8 easy
- Core/breathing: Tall-kneeling pressout 2x8; 2–3 min side-lying breathing

Cardio (Week 11)
- 2 sessions, 20–25 min easy (RPE 3–4); prefer pool or bike. No surges.

Week 12 (Safe “peak” week; no true 1RMs)
- Heavier singles/doubles at RPE 7–8 to showcase strength; estimate 1RM from submax sets. Spotters/safeties set. Exhale through effort.

Day A (Squat + press)
- Hatfield or SSB box squat
  - Work to single @ RPE 7; optional single @ RPE 8 if crisp
  - Back-off 2x3 @ RPE 6–7
  - Estimate 1RM from single or 3s using E1RM calculation
- Press: Incline machine or DB press
  - 1–2 top sets of 1–2 reps @ RPE 7–8
  - Back-off 2x4–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Core/carry: Suitcase carry 3x20–25 m/side; Pallof press 2x20 s/side

Day B (Hinge + upper)
- Trap-bar deadlift (high handles) or block pulls
  - Single @ RPE 7; optional single @ RPE 8
  - Back-off 2x2–3 @ RPE 6–7
  - Estimate 1RM from single
- Pull/press accessories: Lat pulldown 3x6–8 @ RPE 7; landmine or seated press 3x5–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Core: Incline dead bug 2x5/side; offset carry 2x20 m/side

Day C (Total-body showcase)
- Landmine squat to target: 2x2 @ RPE 7–8; then 1x3–5 @ RPE 6–7
- RDL: 2x4–6 @ RPE 6–7 (2–3 s eccentric)
- Row + shoulder accessory: 2–3x8 each, moderate
- Optional 5–6 min easy sled pushes

Cardio (Week 12)
- 2 sessions, 25–32 min easy-moderate (RPE 4). Keep environment cool and hydration high.

Core focus in Phase 3 and Peak Week
- Maintain anti-extension/anti-rotation with shorter levers and isometrics.
- Example menu this week: Tall-kneeling pressout, Pallof ISO, incline dead bug short lever, offset/suitcase carries, side-lying hip abduction. Keep RPE 6–7.

Upper-body pressing integration summary (across phases)
- Phase 1: Landmine press, machine incline press, seated DB OHP (back-supported).
- Phase 2: Pressing gets top sets/back-offs: landmine press, incline machine/DB press, seated/Arnold press; density mini-blocks optional.
- Phase 3: Maintain with supported presses, moderate RPE; Week 12 includes submax singles/doubles on incline press for a “test” feel.

Conditioning fuel and recovery highlights
- On higher-intensity Phase 2 days, bias carbs up (4–5 g/kg); pre-lift 30–50 g carbs + 20–25 g protein; post 25–35 g protein + 60–90 g carbs.
- Sleep 7–9 hours; cool training space; supportive footwear; consider belly support band for longer walks.
- If pelvic girdle symptoms arise: shorten strides, choose cycling/swimming, increase support on single-leg work, add adductor mini-ball squeezes (2x12 gentle).

Autoregulation and substitutions
- Swap any uncomfortable move for a listed alternative in the same pattern:
  - Squat: Goblet/landmine/leg press/Hatfield-to-box
  - Hinge: Trap-bar DL, block pulls, RDL, cable pull-through
  - Press: Incline machine/DB, landmine, seated machine/OHP, side-lying DB press
  - Pull: Assisted pull-up/pulldown, chest-supported row
  - Core: Choose from anti-extension/anti-rotation/carries list
- Keep RPE caps, clean bar speed, and stop if symptoms or coning appear.

This plan keeps her training hard-but-smart, maintains lean mass and strength, satisfies her love of pressing, progressively challenges the core, integrates cardio and nutrition, and culminates in a safe, motivating peak in Week 12 without maximal attempts.

Below is the complete 12-week prenatal program for your advanced lifter (starting ~20 weeks pregnant), integrating all adjustments: prenatal safeguards, strength phases, higher-intensity Phase 2, robust upper-body pressing that preserves the “bench” feel without supine, progressive core plan, integrated cardio, nutrition to maintain lean mass, and a safe “peak” Week 12. Three primary strength days plus an optional Day D. All intensities guided by RPE, talk test, and daily autoregulation.

Global prenatal guidelines
- No supine after week 16. Use incline, side-lying, half/tall-kneeling, seated, standing.
- No true max attempts. Keep key sets ≤RPE 7–8 (2–3 reps in reserve), no grinders or prolonged Valsalva.
- Stop and refer if red flags: vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, painful contractions, dizziness/faintness, chest pain, calf pain/swelling, shortness of breath at rest, decreased fetal movement.
- Breathing/bracing: 360° breath, gentle brace, exhale on effort.
- Core safety: Avoid aggressive flexion/rotation under load and long front planks/sit-ups; use anti-extension/anti-rotation and carries.
- Session length: 50–70 minutes, including warm-up/cooldown.

Weekly structure
- Day A: Lower-body squat emphasis + push + core
- Day B: Upper emphasis + hinge + core
- Day C: Total body + carries + conditioning
- Optional Day D: Mobility/core/cardio easy (20–35 min)

Warm-up template (10–12 min each session)
- 2–3 minutes 360° diaphragmatic breathing with 3–5 gentle Kegels coordinated with exhale; full relax on inhale.
- Mobility: Cat-cow to neutral, side-lying open books, quadruped T-spine rotations, 90/90 hip switches.
- Activation: Bodyweight sit-to-stand, band lateral walks, scap wall slides.
- Ramp sets: 2–3 progressive sets for first two compounds.

Cardio overview (2–4 days/week)
- Intensity: Conversational pace (RPE 4–5). Short controlled pickups where listed. Avoid overheating.
- Duration: 20–35 minutes/session (up to 40 if feeling great).
- Deload: Reduce volume in Weeks 6 and 11.
- Modalities: Incline walk, upright/recumbent bike, elliptical, pool, easy rowing, steady sled push.

Nutrition overview (lean mass focused; confirm specifics with OB/RD)
- Energy: +300–350 kcal/day in 2nd trimester; +450 kcal/day in 3rd, adjusted to OB weight-gain targets.
- Protein: 1.2–1.6 g/kg/day, distributed 4–5 feedings/day (25–35 g per meal).
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day; higher end on lifting days, pre/post-lift focus.
- Fats: 25–35% calories, prioritize mono/polyunsaturated; include omega-3s.
- Hydration: 2.3–2.7 L/day baseline + sweat; electrolytes on hot/sweaty days.
- Key micros/supplements with OB approval: Prenatal vitamin; iron if indicated; vitamin D per labs; choline ~450 mg/day; DHA 200–300 mg/day (low-mercury fish or algae oil); calcium ~1,000 mg/day; magnesium if needed.
- Training fuel: Pre 30–50 g carbs + 20–25 g protein; post 25–35 g protein + 60–90 g carbs.

Core and pelvic floor principles
- 10–15 min core per lift day: 1 anti-extension, 1 anti-rotation, 1 carry/hip stability.
- Pelvic floor 3–4x/week: 5–8 gentle contractions/day (3–5 s on, 6–8 s relax) + 3–5 quick flicks. Emphasize full relaxation.
- Regress if coning/doming, pelvic heaviness, or pain.

PHASE 1 (Weeks 1–4, ~20–23 weeks): Strength maintenance, posture, patterning
RPE mostly 6–7, smooth reps. Cardio base building.

Week 1
Day A
- Safety bar box squat or goblet squat: 4x5 @ RPE 6
- Split squat: 3x8/side
- 45° back extension (neutral): 3x10
- Seated cable row (neutral): 4x8
- Half-kneeling landmine press: 4x6/side
- Core: Incline dead bug heel taps 3x6/side; Pallof hold 3x20–30s/side
- Optional finisher: Sled push 6x20 m easy-moderate

Day B
- Trap-bar deadlift (high handles): 4x4–5 @ RPE 6–7
- Half-kneeling single-arm lat pulldown: 3x10/side
- Machine chest press slight incline: 4x8
- Tall-kneeling face pull + ER: 3x12
- Suitcase carry: 4x25–35 m/side
- Core: Incline dead bug 3x6/side slow

Day C
- Double KB front rack box squat: 5x5 moderate
- Romanian deadlift: 3x8
- One-arm cable row (split stance): 3x10/side
- Seated DB overhead press (back-supported): 3x8
- Core: Tall-kneeling anti-extension pressout 3x8; carry light front rack 3x20 m

Cardio (Week 1)
- Session 1: Incline walk 25 min, RPE 4 (5 x 3 min steady / 2 min easy)
- Session 2: Bike 20–25 min steady, RPE 4
- Optional Session 3: Pool 20–25 min easy

Week 2
- Progress 2–3% load or +1 rep where RPE allows.
Day A
- SSB box squat: 4x5
- Front-foot elevated split squat: 3x10/side
- Chest-supported row: 4x8
- Half-kneeling landmine press: 4x6–8/side
- Core: Incline dead bug with mini-band 3x6/side; Pallof to overhead reach 3x8/side

Day B
- Rack pull from knee: 4x5
- Single-arm cable chest press (split stance): 3x10/side
- Assisted pull-up or pulldown: 4x6–8
- Suitcase carry: 4x30 m/side
- Core: Quadruped heel slides 3x6/side

Day C
- Landmine goblet squat: 4x6
- KB deadlift: 3x10
- Seated DB overhead press: 3x8–10
- Farmer carry: 4x30 m
- Core: Tall-kneeling pressout 3x8; side-lying abduction 3x12/side

Cardio (Week 2)
- Add 3–5 total minutes across sessions; optional 4 x 45 s brisk pickups on the walk (RPE 5) with 2 min easy.

Week 3
- Slight volume bump; big lifts 5x4–5 at same RPE.
- Add anti-rotation march: Pallof march 3x8/side.
- Keep conditioning steady-state 15–20 min post or separate.

Day A
- SSB box squat: 5x4–5
- Split squat: 4x8/side (3010 tempo)
- Chest-supported row: 4x8–10
- Landmine press with 1–2 s pause: 4x6/side
- Core: Incline dead bug 4x5/side; Pallof march 3x8/side

Day B
- Trap-bar deadlift: 5x4 @ RPE 6–7
- Machine incline chest press: 4x8
- Half-kneeling single-arm pulldown: 3x10/side
- Face pulls: 3x12–15
- Suitcase carry: 4x25–35 m/side
- Core: Tall-kneeling pressout 3x8 slow

Day C
- Landmine squat to target: 5x5
- RDL: 3x8 (3 s eccentric)
- One-arm cable row: 3x10/side
- Seated DB overhead press: 3x8
- Core: Side-lying clamshell 3x12/side; front rack carry 3x20 m

Cardio (Week 3)
- Elliptical 30 min steady, walk 28–30 min with 6 x 1 min brisk (RPE 5), optional swim 25–30 min.

Week 4
- Consolidate: Maintain Week 3 volume, hold or reduce load 2% to keep RPE 6–7.
- Technique: 3–1–1 tempo on RDL and split squats. Monitor diastasis cues.

Day A
- Goblet squat to box: 4x6
- Split squat: 3x10/side (tempo)
- Chest-supported row: 3x8–10
- Landmine press: 3x6/side
- Core: Incline dead bug 3x6/side; Pallof hold 3x25–30s/side

Day B
- Trap-bar DL: 4x4 easy-moderate
- Assisted pull-up or pulldown: 4x6–8
- Incline machine chest press: 3x10 @ 3010
- Suitcase carry: 3x25–30 m/side
- Core: Tall-kneeling pressout 3x8; side-lying abduction 3x12/side

Day C
- Landmine squat: 4x6
- RDL: 3x8 (control)
- Seated DB overhead press: 3x8
- Row variation: 3x10
- Core: Pallof with lateral steps 3x8/side; carry complex light 2 rounds

Cardio (Week 4)
- Hold durations and RPE; add 1–2 min/session only if energy great.

PHASE 2 (Weeks 5–8, ~24–27 weeks): Higher intensity, top sets + back-offs, tempos, density
One primary lift per day gets a top set at RPE 7–8; others RPE 6–7 with tempos/pauses. Short finishers optional.

Week 5
Day A
- Safety bar box squat to parallel
  - Top set 4–5 @ RPE 7–8; back-off 3x4–5 @ RPE 6–7
- DB walking lunge (short stride): 3x10/side @ RPE 7 last reps
- Hip thrust on incline bench: 4x8 @ 3010, RPE 7
- Chest-supported row: 4x8 @ RPE 7
- Press: Half-kneeling landmine press
  - Top set 6 @ RPE 7–8; back-off 3x6 @ RPE 6–7
- Core density (8 min): EMOM alt—Pallof ISO 25–30s/side; anti-rotation march 10 steps

Finisher (6–8 min): Sled push 20 m moderate x 6–8
